statement: The function returns a result r, and r is the minimum, over all permutations p = (p(0),...,p(n-1)) of the index set {0,...,n-1}, of T(p) = sum_{j=0}^{n-1} ceil(strength[p(j)] / (1 + j*k)), where ceil(a/b) for positive integer b and integer a is the least integer t >= 0 with t*b >= a.
preconditions: Let n = len(strength). Assume 1 <= n <= 8, 1 <= k <= 10, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= strength[i] <= 1000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r >= min_{0 <= i < n} strength[i] + (n - 1).
preconditions: Let n = len(strength). Assume 1 <= n <= 8, 1 <= k <= 10, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= strength[i] <= 1000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r >= sum_{i=0}^{n-1} ceil(strength[i] / (1 + (n-1)*k)), where ceil(a/b) is the least integer t >= 0 with t*b >= a.
preconditions: Let n = len(strength). Assume 1 <= n <= 8, 1 <= k <= 10, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= strength[i] <= 1000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r <= sum_{i=0}^{n-1} ceil(strength[i] / (1 + i*k)), where ceil(a/b) is the least integer t >= 0 with t*b >= a.
preconditions: Let n = len(strength). Assume 1 <= n <= 8, 1 <= k <= 10, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= strength[i] <= 1000000.

statement: For every index m with 0 <= m < n and strength[m] = min_{0 <= i < n} strength[i], whenever the function returns a result r, r <= strength[m] + sum_{0 <= i < n, i != m} ceil(strength[i] / (1 + k)), where ceil(a/b) is the least integer t >= 0 with t*b >= a.
preconditions: Let n = len(strength). Assume 1 <= n <= 8, 1 <= k <= 10, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= strength[i] <= 1000000.

statement: If find_minimum_time(a,k) returns r_a and find_minimum_time(b,k) returns r_b, then r_a = r_b.
preconditions: Let a and b be two strength slices of the same length n. Assume 1 <= n <= 8, 1 <= k <= 10, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= a[i] <= 1000000 and 1 <= b[i] <= 1000000. Assume b is a permutation of a, meaning there is a bijection sigma on {0,...,n-1} with b[j] = a[sigma(j)] for every j.

statement: If find_minimum_time(a,k) returns r_a and find_minimum_time(b,k) returns r_b, then r_a <= r_b.
preconditions: Let a and b be two strength slices of the same length n. Assume 1 <= n <= 8, 1 <= k <= 10, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= a[i] <= b[i] <= 1000000.

statement: If find_minimum_time(strength,k1) returns r1 and find_minimum_time(strength,k2) returns r2, then r2 <= r1.
preconditions: Let strength be a slice with n = len(strength). Assume 1 <= n <= 8 and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= strength[i] <= 1000000. Let k1 and k2 satisfy 1 <= k1 <= k2 <= 10.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = min_{0 <= i < n} strength[i] + (n - 1).
preconditions: Let n = len(strength). Assume 1 <= n <= 8, 1 <= k <= 10, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= strength[i] <= 1000000. Assume in addition that strength[i] <= 1 + k for every i with 0 <= i < n.

statement: The function returns a result r (it does not fail), and 1 <= r <= 8000000; more sharply, r <= sum_{i=0}^{n-1} strength[i].
preconditions: Let n = len(strength). Assume 1 <= n <= 8, 1 <= k <= 10, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= strength[i] <= 1000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, there exists a permutation p = (p(0),...,p(n-1)) of the index set {0,...,n-1} such that r = sum_{j=0}^{n-1} ceil(strength[p(j)] / (1 + j*k)) and strength[p(0)] = min_{0 <= i < n} strength[i], where ceil(a/b) for positive integer b and integer a is the least integer t >= 0 with t*b >= a.
preconditions: Let n = len(strength). Assume 1 <= n <= 8, 1 <= k <= 10, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= strength[i] <= 1000000.
